caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates coverage as a function of the number of completions (k), with the x-axis labeled "Number of completions (k)" on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, and the y-axis labeled "Coverage" ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. Four data series are presented: a solid blue line with circular markers for "Llama-3B", a dashed green line with triangular markers for "Llama-3B + FT", a solid light blue line with circular markers for "Llama-1B", and a dashed light green line with triangular markers for "Llama-1B + FT". The "Llama-3B" line starts at approximately 0.42 coverage at k=2^0 and increases to approximately 0.92 at k=2^8. The "Llama-3B + FT" line begins at approximately 0.42 at k=2^0 and reaches approximately 0.92 at k=2^8, remaining nearly parallel and overlapping with the "Llama-3B" line throughout. The "Llama-1B" line starts at approximately 0.22 at k=2^0 and increases to approximately 0.72 at k=2^8, showing a plateau after k=2^7. The "Llama-1B + FT" line begins at approximately 0.22 at k=2^0 and rises to approximately 0.72 at k=2^8, remaining consistently above the "Llama-1B" line by approximately 0.05 coverage across the entire range.
